registry_info.name: selection_garden
registry_info.description: A synthesis artifact for the `selection` family (drift - uniform - culled - runaway - split). One founding population run under all five regimes to the same generation count, so the regimes can be measured against each other instead of met one at a time in five rooms on five different populations.
registry_info.note: Per-token registry file so parallel builders never share one JSON. The five plot names are PRELOADED from non_teleological_evolution.gd at runtime and validated at _ready in both directions; do not retype them here or in the script.

selection_garden.name: Selection Garden
selection_garden.description: One founding population, ten lineages drawn once from a fixed hash and sorted by founding rank, run under all five of the `selection` family's regimes to the SAME six generations and stood side by side on one apron. A blade is a lineage; its height and its colour are its trait, on a scale that does not move between plots. drift has no fitness function at all and is the null hypothesis; uniform is one reward run to completion, which spends the variety without moving the mean; culled is truncation without replacement, so three of ten are left standing on bare ground; runaway is positive feedback, the slope of selection growing with how far the mean has already been carried; split is disruptive selection plus assortative mating, which is what it takes for two morphs to survive. `variation` sets how much heritable spread the regimes are given - at `none` all five plots are ONE photograph, because with no variance there is nothing to select on. `evidence` sets how much proof is standing that the five plots share one origin: nothing, the founder of each lineage on its own blade, or that plus a fixed gauge and the two means ruled across the rank. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing is random.
selection_garden.qfep_connection: A fitness function is somebody's decision about what a good body is, and the five plots are five different somebodies. Standing them on ONE founding population makes the authorship visible: the material is identical, so everything that differs is the taste. The plot that matters most is `drift`, which has no taste at all - and which, on this seed, carried the population further than three of the four tastes did. The ladder of progress is not readable off the outcome.
selection_garden.relationships: Synthesis of the `selection` family - evolved_creatures, evolving_flowers, evolvingflowers, non_teleological_evolution, evolutionary_algorithms, particle_randomness_evolutionary - whose word and value list it reads out of non_teleological_evolution.gd at runtime rather than retyping. Sibling in argument to noise_quarry, which does the same thing for the `readout` family's B dialect: one subject, the family word exhibited rather than swept, and the axes varying what the word is applied to.

spatial_needs.footprint_note: The apron is 6.47 m across five 1.15 m plots with four 0.13 m gaps and two 0.10 m margins, and 0.46 m deep. Seven cells of run, one of depth. The clearance is asked at the front because everything the artifact draws faces the approach and the five plots are meant to be read in one sweep of the eye, left to right, in the family's declared order.

dna.axis_shape:
THE FAMILY WORD IS EXHIBITED, NOT SWEPT, because its values sit SIDE BY SIDE and that is provable from the members' code rather than asserted.

non_teleological_evolution._spawn_population() is a five-branch `match` whose arms call _spawn_uniform / _spawn_culled / _spawn_runaway / _spawn_split / _spawn_initial_population - five different builders, none of which calls another. evolvedcreatures sets `_active_count = CULLED_SLOTS.size() if selection == "culled" else POPULATION_SIZE` and then selects ONE body plan of five from a second `match`. evolvingflowers is the same shape a third time. No value's geometry contains another's and no value is another plus a mark, so there is no top rung that would stand for the rest. Parallel values are exactly the case where showing them all at once is the object, so the word stands - five plots, lettered on the apron - and the axes vary the RUN.

`variation` is a MONOTONE LADDER: none < narrow < wide is one quantity, larger. Not a nesting (the wide founding set does not contain the narrow one; it is the same hash draw scaled by a different half-spread) and not parallel (the rungs are ordered, and the bottom one is degenerate by construction). It must be read in order.

`evidence` nests in the ordinary way, and _build() shows it: the founder ghost is added under `if evidence != "result"` and the gauge under `if evidence == "longhand"`. No rung removes a mark an earlier rung drew, and the five populations are identical at all three. Its tail is a ceiling, not a case.
dna.default: variation=wide, evidence=longhand. A SYNTHESIS HAS NO SHIPPED PLACEMENTS, so there is no pre-promotion behaviour to preserve and the default is a free design choice with a duty only to be the strongest single reading. wide is where all five regimes reach their characteristic end states and where the argument is legible from the doorway; longhand is the only rung that turns the response to selection from an impression into a length against a fixed scale. Checked: no map, no sequence and no cluster file names this token, so nothing is repainted by either choice.
dna.was: nothing. This token did not exist before this pass. The five regimes existed only one at a time, each on its OWN population in its own room - evolvedcreatures' 20 bipeds, evolvingflowers' 16 flowers, non_teleological_evolution's 30 dots - so the one question the family exists to ask, whether a difference between two of these pictures is the regime or the population, could not be put. The founding set was never shared and never shown.
dna.kin:
`selection` is declared by SIX artifacts in two vocabularies, and the split is a SUBSET, not a disagreement. Four declare drift|uniform|culled|runaway|split (evolved_creatures, evolving_flowers, evolvingflowers, non_teleological_evolution); two declare the same list WITHOUT `runaway` (evolutionary_algorithms and particle_randomness_evolutionary, which are ONE scene under two lookup names). The fuller list is taken here, character for character, and it is read at runtime out of SELECTION_SRC.SELECTIONS rather than retyped - non_teleological_evolution.gd is the owner (evolutionary_algorithms' own note says so: "The word `selection` is non_teleological_evolution's") and it is safe to preload because it carries no class_name, no preload and no reference to a global class.

WHY THE TWO DROP `runaway`: they CANNOT express it, and they said so on the record before this pass. Their note refuses the value in as many words - there `runaway` means the population standing at its own max_population ceiling with the field paved, and that population is a fixed 100 bodies which neither reproduces nor grows, so the value could only have been renamed to mean something else, which is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary. A recorded refusal, not an oversight. This garden CAN express it, because its population reproduces, so it stands the plot.

`evidence` is the second family word, 45 declarations across the corpus. The three-rung sub-list result|trace|longhand is taken (ftc_bridge, zeno_staircase, sine_wave_controller, generator_bench, weather_vector_field, calder_mobile, calder_object_mobile, noise_quarry). It should be expected to measure LIKE those siblings, and it is declared second for that reason: it is apparatus, not the subject.

genetic_tree_sculptor took `pressure` (none|reach|spread|thicket|spare) rather than `selection`, on the ground that three of selection's five values are POPULATION pictures and that artifact is one tree on a pedestal. That refusal is upheld here and cuts the other way: this IS a population picture, five of them, so `selection` is the right word and `pressure` would be the wrong one.
dna.declines:
`generations` DECLINED, and this is the brief's own instruction as well as the right call: every plot runs to GENERATIONS = 6. Sweeping it would photograph the clock instead of the regime, and the family has refused the same knob twice already (genetic_tree_sculptor's `generations` - "a gen-20 and a gen-40 climb under one taste land on the same tree"; evolvingflowers' `generation_time`, a 3-to-30-second clock).

`evidence = axiom` DECLINED. The axiom rung, where six siblings carry it, shows the RULE the picture obeys - a stated law the geometry is an instance of. This garden's arithmetic is a fitness function per plot, which is five rules, not one, and there is no equation the five share that is not simply "a population reproduces". A rung that would have to print five different formulae is a legend, not a ladder.

THE FAMILY'S PER-VALUE HUES DECLINED. non_teleological_evolution carries UNIFORM_HUE, CULLED_HUE, RUNAWAY_HUE and two SPLIT hues, and lipping each plot in its own value's colour was the obvious tribute. It is refused because the five plots here must differ ONLY by what their populations did: a colour keyed to the plot's NAME would hand the eye a difference the experiment did not produce, and `drift` has no hue constant to borrow anyway (its founders are randomly coloured by construction). Colour in this garden carries the trait and nothing else. The word is carried by the lettering instead.

A SIXTH `founding` AXIS DECLINED - the shape of the founding distribution (uniform / peaked / bimodal). Real, photographable, and it would have made the sweep 3 x 3 x 3, of which build_dna_gallery renders only the first two axes at all.
dna.curriculum_honesty: CHECKED, because the corpus rule is that a room may only use concepts the player has walked. This artifact's sequence is machinelearning, order 20 of 24 in commons/maps/curriculum_spine.json; randomness is order 10 and noise is 11. Both are ten sequences behind, so an argument that leans on sampling, drift and mutation is standing on ground the player has already crossed. Worth stating anyway: there is no randf, no randi and no randomize in this file at all - every draw is an integer hash of (generation, slot), so what the player meets is a fixed object, not a sample.
dna.one_arithmetic: The founding set is computed ONCE per build, in _founders(), and passed to all five plots. _run_regime() is ONE function called five times; the only thing that differs between the calls is the weight vector _fitness() returns, plus the one place `split` touches the parent POOL. THE PARENT-CHOICE AND MUTATION HASHES ARE NOT KEYED ON THE REGIME - _u01(100 + t, 1, j) and _u01(200 + t, 2, j) - so the five plots are one founding population under ONE sequence of chance with five weightings on it. That is what makes `drift` the literal control for the other four: whatever drift did, they all did, plus their selection. The first version keyed the stream on the regime index and the garden was five experiments instead of one; the difference is invisible in a still and total in what the still means.
dna.measured_in_python:
The model is re-implemented in Python and run before any geometry existed, because an exhibit of five regimes that turn out to look alike is a finished-looking experiment that answers nothing. It found two faults and one finding.

FAULT 1: `split` DID NOT SPLIT. Disruptive fitness w = exp(9 * |x - 0.5|) with whole-population roulette went UNIMODAL - at wide it ended at a mean of 0.7967 against runaway's 0.7967, the same number to four places, two plots that were one photograph. The cause is real biology, not a bug: with N = 10 the heavier tail wins outright. Assortative mating (the parent pool restricted to the parent's own side of MID) is the textbook requirement for two morphs to survive disruptive selection, and adding it is what makes `split` split - 6 low at 0.226..0.268 against 4 high at 0.805..0.844. It is stated in the code as part of what the word names rather than hidden in a fitness curve bent until the picture came out.

FAULT 2: the founder ghost measured 3.80% focus against the blade it stands on at variation=none - under the 6% twin bar - because Color(0.60, 0.61, 0.63) and a mid-trait blade have almost the same luminance and the critic scores luminance. Lifting it to bone (0.88, 0.89, 0.84) and giving it a cap that overhangs the blade in x moved that pair to 16.10%.

THE FINDING, which is the artifact's hardest sentence and was not designed in: DRIFT OUTRAN THREE OF THE FOUR PRESSURES, at BOTH live rungs. Response of the mean against the founding mean of 0.5000 - at wide: drift +0.1979, uniform -0.0071, culled +0.1721, runaway +0.3425, split -0.0199. At narrow: drift +0.0660, uniform +0.0021, culled +0.0574, runaway +0.1009, split +0.0032. Only runaway beat the null hypothesis. Drift's signature is not that it went nowhere - it is that it went somewhere RAGGED: Wright-Fisher resampling at N = 10 loses (1 - 1/10)^6 = 53% of the founding heterozygosity to coalescence, so its rank ends as three repeated levels (six blades at 0.78..0.83, two at 0.38..0.40, two at 0.70..0.71) where runaway's is one flat level at 0.824..0.865. Texture, not height, is what tells them apart, and a visitor who reads only the mean cannot tell them apart at all. That is the point of standing the null hypothesis in the row.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in the critic's own currency: crop to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralise each frame against its own corner pixel, greyscale, resize to 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5%. Rasterised in Python at the sweep's own rig (FOV 34, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, PAD 1.9, RES 760, framing 0.55); the subject crop measures 622 x 221 = 137,462 px.

THE CLOSEST PAIR IS `evidence` trace vs longhand AT variation=none, 10.25% focus / 0.51% frame.

THE ARITHMETIC. At variation=none every founder equals every plot's final trait, so the founding mean and all five final means are 0.5000 and longhand's two mean rails COINCIDE. The bone rail sits 0.042 m behind the accent one: at this standpoint that is 0.5811 x 0.042 = 0.0244 m of screen-x (2.7 px) and 0.2660 x 0.81388 x 0.042 = 0.0091 m of sight-line drop (1.0 px), so the accent rail hides all but a sliver of it. What longhand adds beyond trace is therefore five stiles (3.64 x 92.2 px = 336 px each), 25 ticks (5.55 x 2.73 px = 15.2 px each) and effectively ONE visible rail per plot (89.3 x 2.85 px = 254 px) instead of two: 5 x (336 + 5 x 15.2 + 254) = 3,830 px, which is 2.79% of the crop. That is under the 5% focus pool, so the pool is diluted with unchanged pixels and the hottest-5% mean lands near (2.79 / 5) x the per-pixel delta.

AXIS MEANS PREDICTED: variation 23.72% focus (closest pair none vs narrow at longhand, 14.11%), evidence 18.98% focus. Both above the 12% WEAK bar; nothing under the 3% INERT bar; nothing under the 6% twin bar.

READ EVERY NUMBER ABOVE AS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. A Python rasteriser has one directional light, flat shading and no shadows, ambient occlusion or antialiasing, and the four predictions in the corpus that named a pair and a number under-predicted by 1.5x, 1.7x, 3.5x and 6.7x. The rule that makes this a gate: IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW THESE NUMBERS, SOMETHING IS BROKEN. One known bias in the other direction: the raster does not draw the five Label3D words, which are identical in every tile and add unchanged pixels inside the crop, so the real focus figures are diluted slightly relative to these - a few tenths of a point, not a factor.
dna.framing_why:
DERIVED FROM THE UNION AABB ACROSS ALL NINE FRAMES, not from the default. The union is 6.47 x 0.93 x 0.46 centred at (0, 0.465, 0.07): x is the apron, y runs from the apron's underside to the top of a longhand stile, z from the plot slabs' back edge to the apron's lettering strip. Diagonal sqrt(41.8609 + 0.8649 + 0.2116) = 6.55266, radius 3.27633. The rig is dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) x PAD x framing with FOV 34 and PAD 1.9, so framing 1.0 would stand the camera at 3.27633 / 0.305731 x 1.9 = 20.361 m and show a 12.450 m frame around a 6.47 m object - PAD already shows 1.9x the bounding radius, which is why a long low bench wants framing well under 1.0.

AT 0.55 the camera comes to 11.1986 m and the frame to 6.84753 m, i.e. 110.99 px per metre. The subject's projected width is 6.47 x 0.81388 + 0.46 x 0.58104 = 5.26580 + 0.26728 = 5.53308 m, 80.80% of frame width, with 0.657 m (72.9 px) of clear margin each side. Cropping is arithmetically impossible above framing = 1 / PAD = 0.52632 because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE, so 0.55 keeps 4.5% of sphere margin in hand for the showcase key light's specular fringe, which the replica does not model.

SUBJECT SHARE IS 4.73% to 5.94% ACROSS THE NINE TILES and that is NOT a framing fault - it is taxonomy_hall's case. The union box fills 80.80% of frame width; the garden is simply airy, fifty 5.96 px blades and two mean rails on a 0.05 m apron. The bar that matters is BLANK_SUBJECT = 0.2%, and every tile clears it by more than twenty times. Tightening below 0.53 would buy about half a point of subject share and spend the entire crop margin, so it was not done.

GAUGE CHECK AT 110.99 px/m, because foresight_range shipped 0.028 m arrows onto an 18 m lane. Screen widths use |right.x| = 0.81388 and |right.z| = 0.58104; verticals use cos(pitch) = 0.96644 plus 0.20925 for depth.
  blade            5.96 px wide;  pitch 8.85 px, so a 2.89 px gap
  tallest blade   86.9 px;  shortest (trait 0) 9.65 px
  0.1 of trait     7.72 px of height - the smallest difference the axis has to show
  founder ghost    3.85 px wide, up to 86.9 px tall
  founder cap      9.16 px wide (1.60 px of overhang each side of the blade), 2.52 px thick
  gauge stile      3.64 px wide, 92.2 px tall
  level tick       5.55 px long, 2.73 px thick
  mean rail       89.3 px long, 2.85 px thick
  lettering       11.5 px em
The thinnest marks in the garden are the level tick at 2.73 px, the mean rail at 2.85 px and the blade gap at 2.89 px. Nothing is under two pixels; the one-to-three pixel band that has sunk axes elsewhere was designed out by choosing the pitch from the screen arithmetic rather than from the plan.
dna.z_stack:
WRITTEN OUT BEFORE THE BUILD, because operations_gallery's bezel was a solid slab enclosing every mark its axis drew and photographed blank at 70.3% subject. Depths, from the back of the bed forward: plot slab -0.120..+0.120; blade -0.007..+0.007; founder ghost +0.007..+0.019; founder cap +0.007..+0.023; final-mean rail +0.044..+0.056; founding-mean rail +0.086..+0.098; gauge stile -0.010..+0.010. Everything the axes draw is IN FRONT of the blade it comments on or beside it, and everything sits inside the plot slab's own z span, so nothing overhangs the bed.

THE ONE MARK THAT WAS MOVED. The founding-mean rail was first hung 0.09 m BEHIND the rank, which reads well in plan and is invisible in the frame: a sight line here descends 0.2660 m per metre of ground travel, so 0.09 m of standoff buys 0.0195 m of clearance and every blade taller than 0.4815 m hides the rail behind it - which at wide is most of runaway's rank and, since blades occupy 5.96 of every 8.85 px of pitch, 67% of the rail's length. Both rails now stand in front. They cost a 2.85 px band of every blade they cross, which is what a mean line is supposed to look like.

SCREEN-X CLEARANCES, since removal_room's three registers overlapped by 33.5% of a register's width at its inherited pitch. Blade to blade: 8.85 px of pitch against 5.96 px of blade, 2.89 px clear. Gauge stile to the first blade: 10.3 px between centres against 1.82 + 2.98 px of half-widths, 5.5 px clear. Tick tabs point LEFT into the 0.13 m plot gap and their outer edge lands 0.221 m (20.0 px) clear of the previous plot's last blade; pointing them right would have put a 0.05 m tab 0.033 m from the first blade's centre, i.e. inside it.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED KEY IS NEEDED, and it is checkable rather than claimed. The file contains no randf, no randi, no randomize, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Tween, no physics body, no await and no reference to the scene tree outside its own children. _ready is UNGATED: it reads config metadata, checks the family list against the preloaded const in both directions, checks its own layout arithmetic, and builds the whole garden from the two @export values alone - so the sweep's rescue path (call apply_grid_config when the AABB measures zero) will never fire.

EVERY DRAW IS AN INTEGER HASH of (generation, slot), stateless and replicable in Python to the bit, which is how dna.predicted_degeneracy is arithmetic on this geometry rather than an estimate. Traits are held in Array[float] and NOT in PackedFloat32Array: the Python model is float64, and rounding every trait to float32 on each write could flip a roulette boundary and make the prediction a statement about a picture the script does not build.

TWO WAYS IN, ONE VALIDATOR EACH. The sweep sets the @export directly before add_child; the grid stamps config_variation / config_evidence metadata, which _read_grid_config_meta walks up the ancestor chain for before _ready builds; and apply_grid_config takes a dictionary. All are validated, and apply_grid_config rebuilds ONLY when a value actually changed AND _ready has already built once - the force_pad fault. An unrecognised word keeps the standing value. BOTH AXES ARE String ENUMS, not bools, so the fixture-string trap (a typed bool rejecting the string "true" before _ready) cannot occur here. curation_station's {"emissive": false} falls straight through and rebuilds nothing, and it is a genuine no-op: no material in this file enables emission.
dna.still_note: Everything both axes change is standing geometry in one frame: a height, a colour, a body present or absent, a mark added. Nothing animates, nothing is grabbable, nothing waits. The six generations are consumed at BUILD time and the photograph is of the outcome, which is exactly why `variation` is admissible where the family's `generation_time` and `energy_decay` are not - the same rate, spent before the shutter rather than during it.
dna.budget: 3 x 3 = 9 variants, which is build_dna_gallery's DEFAULT cap exactly, so nothing is trimmed and the coverage record is complete - the dot_aligner fault (a four-value axis rendered at two and judged as four) cannot occur at this size. `variation` is declared FIRST because the sweep trims the LATER axis from the tail: at any cap of 3 or more it keeps all three rungs, so `wide` - the default and the whole argument - is never at risk. The residual tension is stated rather than hidden: a run at --max=6 would trim `evidence` to result|trace and drop `longhand`, which IS this artifact's default. Do not run this sweep below 9.
dna.known_gap:
NO GODOT RENDER EXISTS YET. Every number in this block is Python: the population model, the projection and the critic's metric, all re-implemented. The declaration gate passes and the geometry arithmetic is written out, but nobody has looked at this artifact, and no verdict about it - alive or dead - should be issued until the sweep has run. If it comes back below dna.predicted_degeneracy, read the harness before reading the design.

AND THE STANDPOINT CAVEAT APPLIES IN ADVANCE. This garden is a rank of thin blades read against their own heights; that is close to a frontal reading, and the sweep's standpoint is 36 degrees off frontal. If any pair comes back flat, run `python tools/probe_anamorphic.py --token=selection_garden --axis=<axis>` before believing it - five of seven dead verdicts in this corpus were false.
